You're redesigning the game-selection step of Nxeon's deploy wizard for Next.js/TypeScript, staging tree at /opt/nxeon-staging — work ONLY in staging, never /opt/nxeon prod. Never run `npm run build`; verify only with `npx tsc --noEmit`.

Context: the deploy wizard's "Choose your game" step (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` — find the exact component/section) currently shows every orderable game as a static grid of cover-art tiles (search for the tile component — likely `GameCoverTile` or similar, possibly with a `GameCoverCarousel` variant already existing per a recent art-sourcing report that mentioned both names — find and read both if they exist). There's already a category filter row (tabs like "All / Building / Sandbox / Shooter / Survival") and a "Popular first" sort dropdown above the grid.

The problem: today, roughly 13 new games are being added to the catalog in parallel (Dragonwilds, Sunkenland, Abiotic Factor, Core Keeper, Icarus, ARK: Survival Ascended, Soulmask, Don't Starve Together, Vintage Story, Necesse, Team Fortress 2, DayZ, Left 4 Dead 2) — the existing static grid already showed ~19 games before these were added, so it'll be pushing 30+ once they land. The owner wants a cleaner, more scalable way to browse this many games — they suggested a sliding carousel as one option, but are open to "some cleaner more organized way" — and were explicit that the individual game cover TILE design itself (the card look — art, name, price, badges) should stay exactly as it is, this is purely about the browsing/layout mechanism around those tiles, not the tiles themselves.

Your job:
1. Read the current implementation fully — the wizard page, the tile component, the category filter logic, the sort logic, and how the game list is fetched/filtered (likely `GAME_FAMILIES.filter(f => withTiers.has(f))` per earlier investigation, plus category tagging).
2. Assess whether category tags exist and are correctly assigned for ALL games (old and any newly-seeded ones you can check) — a scalable browsing UI is only as good as its filtering; if categories are missing/wrong for some games, note or fix that as part of the redesign (e.g. Dragonwilds/Sunkenland/Icarus/Abiotic Factor/Core Keeper should get sensible category tags like "Survival"/"Sandbox" if not already tagged).
3. Design and implement an improved browsing mechanism appropriate for 30+ items. Consider: keeping the existing category tabs + sort as the primary filter (already good), but replacing or augmenting the single long static grid with something that handles scale better — options to weigh: (a) pagination or a "show more" load-more pattern within each category, (b) a horizontal sliding/scrollable carousel per category or for a "Popular"/"New" row up top with the full filtered grid below, (c) a denser grid with virtualization if the list gets very long, (d) a search box (there's already a "Search games..." input visible in the current UI per the screenshot context — confirm it's real/functional, or wire it up if it's just a placeholder). Pick a pragmatic, non-over-engineered solution — this is a marketing-adjacent purchase flow, keep it fast and simple to use, not flashy for its own sake. A good default: keep category tabs + working search + sort as the primary navigation (fastest to find a specific game), and address the "too long a scroll" problem with either pagination or a "Popular" carousel row up top highlighting featured/popular games (using the tile's existing "Popular" badge, visible in the screenshot) followed by the full categorized/searchable grid below.
4. Preserve the exact visual design of individual game tiles — do not redesign the card itself, only how many are shown/how they're navigated.
5. Make sure whatever you build handles the current ~19 games fine visually AND will hold up cleanly once the ~13 new games land (some of which may not have art fully ready yet at the moment you're working — code defensively, don't assume every game has complete art, since a parallel task is still sourcing some of it).
6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, confirm clean.

Report back (under 400 words): what you found (existing search functional or not, category tagging completeness), what you built/changed, and how it holds up at both current scale (~19) and near-future scale (~32). Flag anything you're not fully confident renders well (can't run a dev server here) rather than asserting it's perfect.

## Summary

**File touched:** `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx` (staging only, no prod changes).

**What I found:**
- The "Choose your game" step lives in `GameDeployWizard.tsx` (rendered from `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` → `DeployHub.tsx`), not in the page file directly.
- Search was already fully functional (not a placeholder) — `gameQuery` filters by name/family, with sort (`featured`/`name`/`price`) and category pills all wired and working correctly.
- `GameCoverCarousel` (`components/marketing/showcase/GameCoverCarousel.tsx`) is a separate, much heavier hand-rolled coverflow carousel used only on the public `/game-servers` marketing hero — it's not part of the wizard and I left it untouched (reusing its momentum/physics logic here would have been over-engineering for a purchase flow).
- **Real live bug found**: `lib/games.ts` already has a "Wave 3" of 5 games seeded today (dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, corekeeper, icarus — confirmed live via `prisma/seed-wave3-games.ts` with active `GamePlan` tiers), bringing the current catalog to ~24 games already, past the "~19" baseline in the brief. But the wizard's own `GAME_GENRE` map (which drives the category pills) had no entries for any of these 5, so they were all silently dumping into the generic "Other" bucket — the same class of bug a comment in `lib/games.ts` already documents happening once before with `GAME_DISPLAY`.

**What I changed:**
1. Added `GAME_GENRE` entries: dragonwilds/sunkenland/abioticfactor/icarus → "Survival", corekeeper → "Sandbox" (plus a defensive "schedule1" entry, since it's unseeded but present in `GAME_FAMILIES`).
2. Added a capped "Popular" rail above the toolbar — plain native horizontal scroll with `snap-x`/`snap-mandatory` (no custom JS physics), sourced from the same `featured` tier flag as the existing badge, shown only on the untouched "All + no search" view so it never competes with a customer's own filter.
3. Extracted the tile markup into a `renderGameTile()` plain function (not a nested component — a nested component would get a new identity every render and remount `GameCoverTile`'s image-fallback state on every keystroke) so the rail and the grid share pixel-identical tiles. Tile visuals are byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. Added a "Show all N games" expand button below the main grid, capping the initial render at 12 tiles; resets whenever search/category/sort changes. No pagination state, no URL params — kept intentionally simple per the brief.

**Scale check:** at today's ~24 games, "All" now shows a Popular rail + first 12 tiles + a "Show all 24" button; most single categories (e.g. "Building" with 2 games) render exactly as before, untouched by the cap. Once the ~8 remaining games land (Survival could reach ~18 in one category), the same cap/expand and rail continue to apply without further changes needed.

**Not fully verified (no dev server here):** the horizontal-scroll snap rail's visual spacing/scrollbar look on actual mobile Safari/Chrome — CSS-only and should be robust, but I couldn't screenshot it. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
